title.en: Build dependency graph and topological order

summary: Show a build plan as a directed graph whose valid orders come from its structure, and make a cycle a reported failure.
objective: Build a dependency graph where I can request a topological order, add an edge that creates a cycle and see the cycle reported instead of an order.
intent_signals: Show a valid build order for a dependency graph.
Demonstrate what happens when dependencies form a cycle.
example_prompts: Build a dependency graph with a topological order I can step through and a cycle detector.
Show which targets can be built in parallel because nothing orders them.
negative_signals: Not a build system or scheduler: no durations, resources or caching are modelled.
Not a claim that the shown order is unique; several valid orders usually exist.
not_for: Not a build system or scheduler: no durations, resources or caching are modelled.
Not a claim that the shown order is unique; several valid orders usually exist.

entities.name: Target nodes
entities.guidance: Give each target a node with its name and its direct dependencies listed, so an edge has a readable meaning.

entities.name: Order lane
entities.guidance: Lay the produced order along a lane in space, so a node position in the lane is its rank, not an aesthetic placement.

entities.name: Cycle report
entities.guidance: When a cycle exists, highlight the actual cycle as a closed chain and refuse to produce an order.

state_contract.model: A directed graph whose edges point from dependency to dependent, a topological order computed when the graph is acyclic, and a directed cycle recovered by depth-first search otherwise. Nodes with no directed path between them in either direction are marked as concurrency candidates.
state_contract.authority: The graph is authoritative. The lane layout, the concurrency marking and the cycle highlight are all derived from it and must be recomputed after every edit.
actions: Add or remove a dependency edge.
Request a topological order and step through it.
Introduce a cycle and read the report.

invariants: A produced order places every dependency before its dependent, without exception.

A graph with a directed cycle produces no order at all, and the cycle is found by traversal rather than inferred from the drawing: adding an edge that points backwards along a displayed order is not itself a cycle, since two unrelated nodes can be joined in either direction and stay acyclic.
Nodes marked as concurrent have no directed path between them in either direction.
motion_guidance: Animate the order being built one node at a time so the ordering rule is observable.
Highlight the cycle as a traversal around the closed chain rather than as a static colour change.
known_limits: Several valid topological orders usually exist; the one shown depends on the traversal and tie-breaking rule.
Real build parallelism also depends on resources and durations, which are outside this recipe.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: A directed acyclic graph is a digraph with no directed cycles, a topological order arranges vertices so that every directed edge points from an earlier vertex to a later one, and a digraph has a topological order if and only if it is a directed acyclic graph.
claims.scope: Definitions and the equivalence as cited.

source_refs.locator: 4.2 Directed Graphs, DAG and topological order

claims.statement: Directed cycle detection asks whether a digraph has a directed cycle and can be solved with depth-first search.
claims.scope: Existence of a cycle and its recovery, as cited.

object_craft.structure: Rounded blocks with a name plate and small sockets showing incoming and outgoing edge counts.
object_craft.material: Neutral node material; reserve one accent for the current step and another for cycle members.
object_craft.articulation: Nodes translate into their lane rank when an order is produced and return on reset.

object_craft.structure: A physical rail with numbered slots so rank is countable rather than inferred from spacing.
object_craft.material: Rail material subdued with high-contrast slot numbers.
object_craft.articulation: Slots fill one at a time as the order is stepped.

physical_contract.scope: Graph analysis with animated layout; no physical forces in the layout.
checks: Every edge points forward in the produced order.

In a fixture with an existing directed path A to B, adding B to A produces a cycle and no order. Adding a visually backward edge between unrelated nodes can stay acyclic and must not be rejected without graph traversal.
